title: DSA PREP THAT
ACTUALLY WORKS
pages.takeaway: Volume is not the metric. Variety is.

pages.label: the volume myth
title: 500 PROBLEMS,
STILL STUCK
body: Still froze on the first mock interview.
Solving more does not fix solving wrong.
pages.takeaway: More problems will not save you.

pages.label: the actual fix
title: SOLVE DIFFERENT,
NOT MORE
body: Same problem types on repeat ?= plateau.
Your brain adapts to the pattern.
pages.takeaway: Brain adapts to patterns. Break them.

pages.label: the unexpected topic
title: LLD IS ASKED
IN PLACEMENT
body: It shows up in placement rounds,
LLD is the difference between rounding up
pages.takeaway: Study LLD even if the job posting says coding only.

pages.label: the overrated topic
title: TREES ARE
THE TRAP
body: rarely show up in early interview rounds.

pages.label: the rotation that worked
title: A2Z FOR BREADTH
79 FOR DEPTH
body: A2Z first: broad rotation, high volume.
Then Striver 79: revision after revision until settled.
pages.takeaway: Revision of your errors is the actual learning.

pages.label: the resume trick
title: CORE PROJECTS,
NOT TUTORIALS
body: Do not list AI-powered task managers.
List projects that show architecture decisions:
Interviewers ask how you think, not what tools you installed.

pages.label: teach-as-you-go
title: TEACH DSA TO
LEARN DSA
body: is how you know you understand it.
Say the approach before writing code.
The interviewer only hear your reasoning.
Practice explaining out loud alone in your room.
pages.takeaway: If you cannot explain it, you do not own it.

pages.label: start here  ·  today
title: TOKEN BUDGETS;
ONE CHANGE
body: Do revise one old problem today.
Re-solve a problem you failed last week.
Say it out loud while you do it.
That single exerciseworth more than ten new problems.
